title: Observability Budget and Service Slimming Guidelines
author: Sofia Alvarez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a repeatable program and concrete runbook for managing observability cost at the service level while preserving operational signal. The objective is to cap telemetry spend (the observability budget) per service and to provide a lean, measurable process for "slimming" instrumentation without increasing incident risk.

Scope: applies to all services owned by Platform, Serving Runtime, and Eng Platform teams that emit metrics, traces, or high-cardinality logs to our central observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana, Tempo, Loki, Honeycomb). This is not a replacement for security or compliance auditing of logs.

Owners and Stakeholders
- Program owner: Platform Observability (primary contact: sofia.alvarez@redwood.com)
- Participating teams: eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, infra-costs
- Executive sponsor: VP Platform (for budget escalations)

Goals and Non-Goals\- Goals:
  - Define a per-service monthly observability budget expressed in ingestion units and CPU/egress cost estimates.
  - Provide a 6-step slimming playbook that reduces high-cardinality telemetry and eliminates redundant instrumentation.
  - Map observability changes to SLO impact assessments and rollback criteria.
\- Non-Goals:
  - Eliminating traces or metrics required for security/compliance.
  - Reducing developer visibility below a minimum safety floor.

Terminology
- Observability Budget: a monthly allocation per service measured in ingestion units (metrics*1 + traces*5 + logs*0.2), where coefficients are the finance-backed conversion to USD.
- High-cardinality tag: any label on metrics/logs/traces with more than 100 distinct values/hour.
- Sampling floor: the minimum sampling rate allowed for any given telemetry type (default 10% for traces, 100% for error logs).

How we compute budgets (example)
- Inputs: 30-day baseline ingestion, egress cost, SRE safety margin (15%).
- Example calculation for routing-service (monthly):
  - Baseline metrics: 45M metric samples
  - Baseline traces: 220k traces
  - Baseline logs: 12M log lines
  - Ingestion units = (45M*1) + (220k*5) + (12M*0.2) = 45M + 1.1M + 2.4M = 48.5M units
  - Finance rate = $0.00002 per unit -> budget = $970/month (+15% safety = $1,115)

Service classification and budget tiers
- Tier A (critical infra, e.g., inference-proxy, routing-service): 2x baseline budget, sampling floor 25% for traces, full error logs retained.
- Tier B (high-traffic application services): 1.25x baseline budget, sampling floor 10% for traces.
- Tier C (batch/analytics, non-customer-facing): 0.5x baseline budget, aggressive sampling allowed (1–5%).

Detecting budget violations (automated checks)
1) Daily budget burn-rate alert: Prometheus rule computes 7-day projected spend and fires if >110% of monthly budget.
2) Cardinality bloom: nightly job compares distinct tag counts per metric; raises pager when growth >3x baseline for Tier A.
3) SLI signal-loss estimator: a synthetic probe that measures whether key SLI panels retain >=90% of their historical correlation with incidents (see SLI mapping below).

Slimming Playbook (6 steps)
1) Identify the dominant contributors
   - Run: ./observability-cli top-emitters --service routing-service --window 7d
   - Output shows top metrics/traces/log streams by units and cost.
2) Triage by signal importance
   - Label each emitter as: "critical for SLO", "diagnostic", or "noise".
   - Use the SLO Impact Matrix (table below) with owner sign-off.
3) Apply targeted reductions
   - For metrics: remove per-request high-cardinality tags (request_id, session_token) and switch to histograms for latency buckets. Example Prometheus snippet:

   prometheus_remote_write:
     write_relabel_configs:
       - source_labels: ["route_id"]
         action: replace
         regex: ".*"
         replacement: "redacted"

   - For traces: implement adaptive sampling in the SDK (example for OpenTelemetry Python):

   from opentelemetry import trace
   from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.sampling import TraceIdRatioBased

   sampler = TraceIdRatioBased(0.10)  # 10% baseline, 100% on errors

   - For logs: reduce structured fields with high cardinality; add log sampling policies in Fluentd:

   <filter routing-service.*>
     @type throttle
     key request_path
     rate 200
   </filter>

4) Validate signal preservation
   - Run synthetic incident correlation tests: compare pre/post Pearson correlation between metric X and the incident label (historical window 30d). Threshold: correlation must not drop >15% for Tier A signals.
5) Canary and rollout
   - Canary at 5% of traffic for 1 hour -> 25% for 4 hours -> 100% if no signal degradation or budget alerts.
   - Rollback if: new p99 latency > baseline+10ms AND SLI error rate increase > 0.05% OR budget burn spikes > 25% during canary.
6) Post-change audit and retro
   - Produce a Slimming Report (template below) and schedule a 2-week retro to review if debugging time increased.

SLO Impact Matrix (text table)
Metric/Log/Trace | Critical for SLO? | Allowed reduction | Owner sign-off required
------------------|-------------------|-------------------|-------------------
routing_service.latency_hist_p99 | yes | 0% | runtime-observability
routing_service.request_tags | no | remove session_id, request_id | service-owner
error_trace_sample | yes (errors) | keep 100% of errors, baseline sample rest 10% | eng-sre

Operational Runbook (when slimming causes incidents)
1) Pager event: Observability signal-loss pager (SRE #oncall)
2) Initial checks (5 min):
   - Check daily budget burn alert context in Grafana panel "Observability Budgeting – routing-service".
   - Run quick query: prometheus:sum(rate(routing_service_requests_total[5m])) by (status)
3) Quick rollback steps (10 min):
   - If the change is a config flag, toggle: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/feature-flags/observability-slimming/routing-service/disable 
   - If rollout is via deployment, use kubectl rollout undo deployment/routing-service -n prod --to-revision=<previous>
4) After rollback: capture traces/metrics for the incident, tag as "observability-regression", and open a tracking ticket with the slimming report attached.

Dashboard and Alert Examples
- Prometheus recording rule (example):

  groups:
  - name: observability_budget_rules
    rules:
    - record: observability:monthly_ingestion_units:sum
      expr: sum(ingestion_units_total{service="routing-service"})

- Grafana panels to include:
  - Budget burn (7d projection)
  - Top 10 emitters by ingestion units
  - Synthetic SLI correlation delta (pre/post)

- Alert thresholds:
  - observability_budget_projected_exceed: fires at >110% projected monthly spend (severity: P3)
  - high_cardinality_growth: fires if distinct tag count growth >3x for Tier A (severity: P2)

Metrics to track (minimum set)
- ingestion_units_total (labels: service, emitter_type)
- trace_sampling_rate{service} (gauge)
- distinct_tag_count{metric,service} (gauge)
- budget_projection_percent{service} (gauge)

Back-of-envelope CLI tools and scripts
- Quick top emitters (example):
  - observability-cli top-emitters --service inference-proxy --window 1d --format table
- Compute service budget from baseline:
  - observability-cli compute-budget --service routing-service --baseline 30d --safety-margin 15

Change approval and governance
- Any slimming change for Tier A service requires:
  1) One page change proposal in Confluence with SLO impact matrix
  2) Review sign-off from eng-sre and runtime-observability
  3) A canary plan (traffic %) and rollback criteria
- Tier B: change review by service owner and ops reviewer.
- Tier C: automated changes allowed with post-fact sign-off.

Retrospective and KPIs (30/60/90 day)
- 30d: measure delta in monthly observability cost and count of P1/P2 incidents attributed to signal loss. Goal: <=5% incident increase.
- 60d: measure mean time to diagnose (MTTD) for root causes tied to removed telemetry; goal: no >25% regression vs baseline.
- 90d: stable budgets and updated dashboards embedded in service runbooks.

Slimming Report template (must be attached to post-change ticket)
- Service:
- Change author:
- Date:
- Summary of emitters removed/modified:
- Pre/post ingestion units and USD estimate:
- SLO correlation delta (numbers):
- Canary observations and rollback events (if any):
- Action items and follow-ups:

Roadmap items (Q2–Q4 2026)
- Automatic per-service budget suggestions using ML baseline models.
- SDK integrations that support adaptive, incident-aware sampling (server-side decisions).
- UI in Console: per-service observability budget and cost attribution panel.

Appendix: Example incident case study (summary)
- Incident: "Search latency debugging regression" (2026-01-14)
- Root cause: overzealous tag retention in search-service (per-request token in latency metric).
- Action taken: Replaced token label with route_bucket; implemented 10% trace sampling and increased histogram granularity.
- Outcome: Observability cost -18% month over month; detection time for same class of incidents unchanged.
